questions.q: What question does transformation answer that mapping (Lesson 6) does not?
options: Which Salesforce object is in scope
Who signs off on the final migration plan
How many records exist in the source system
What has to happen to a value so it's actually usable on arrival, not just technically present
questions.explain: Mapping answers where a value goes. Transformation answers what has to happen to the value along the way so it lands in Salesforce in a genuinely usable form.

questions.q: A legacy source stores company names inconsistently ("MCDONALD'S INC" vs. "McDonald's Inc") and some values have stray leading whitespace. Which category of transformation does fixing this fall under?
options: Derived/calculated field transformation
Cleansing
Migration sequencing
Picklist value translation
questions.explain: Cleansing covers mechanical fixes that don't change what the data means — whitespace, inconsistent capitalization, stray characters — as opposed to format standardization or computing a new value.

questions.q: Splitting a single legacy "Full Name" field into Salesforce's First Name and Last Name fields is an example of which kind of transformation?
options: A derived/calculated field produced by a documented business rule
Cleansing
Standardization
Migration sequencing
questions.explain: This isn't a mechanical fix or a format change — it requires a business rule (how to split the name, with documented fallbacks for edge cases) to produce two target values that didn't exist as separate source fields.

questions.q: According to this lesson's general rule, when should a transformation be built as an ongoing Salesforce formula field or Flow rather than handled once in pre-load staging?
options: Whenever the transformation is specific to this one migration and won't be needed again
Never — all transformation must happen in pre-load staging
Only when the transformation needs to stay dynamic for new records going forward, or the original value must be preserved alongside a derived one
Only when the source system cannot export a CSV file
questions.explain: The general rule is: transform before load when the logic is specific to this migration; build it into the org only when the logic has an ongoing business purpose beyond the one-time migration event.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say transformation rules should be written directly alongside the mapping document's per-field entries, not as a separate spec?
options: Because Salesforce enforces a single-document requirement for all migration artifacts
Because transformation rules are not actually needed once the mapping document exists
Because separate documents cannot be reviewed during sign-off
Because a mapping entry without its transformation rule next to it is incomplete — anyone picking it up later can't reproduce the logic or know its edge cases
questions.explain: A mapping entry like 'Full Name → First Name, Last Name' is incomplete without the actual splitting rule next to it — keeping them together is what makes the logic reproducible and its edge cases visible.
